channel.title: Robotics Directory - Educational Robots
channel.description: Browse 290 educational robots in the Robotics Directory. Specs, prices, images and comparison.

item.title: D. Creative DIY ESP32 Robot Dog
item.description: DIY 3D-printed robot dog build powered by ESP32 and controlled by phone; the video covers wiring, ESP32 integration, controller setup, troubleshooting and final testing.

item.title: Leju Robotics ROBAN 2
item.description: Small bipedal humanoid for embodied-AI teaching and development. It comes in Lite and Advanced A/B/C editions built on an RK3588 compute module; the Advanced editions add a 117 TOPS module, a depth camera, LiDAR and autonomous navigation. It has hot-swap batteries and LLM Q&A.

item.title: Pollen Robotics Microduck
item.description: 25 cm open-source biped from Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face that you train yourself with reinforcement learning in simulation. It walks, sits, kicks, picks things up with its beak and can get back up after a fall. Pre-orders opened on 27 August 2026.

item.title: Hiwonder ROSpider
item.description: ROSpider is an all-terrain ROS 2 hexapod platform from Hiwonder with eighteen 35 kg high-voltage bus servos, a 6-DOF robotic arm with gripper, LiDAR, a 3D depth camera, a six-microphone array and an OLED display, running on Jetson or Raspberry Pi. It supports SLAM mapping and navigation, 3D grasping and multimodal large AI models, powered by an 11.1 V 6,000 mAh battery.

item.title: Hiwonder AiMecha M1
item.description: AiMecha M1 is an AI educational robot car from Hiwonder with an all-metal Mecanum-wheel chassis, a 3-DOF vision robotic arm, an ESP32 + MM32 dual-core controller and the K230-based WonderLens Pro AI module with a 1080p camera and 2.4-inch touchscreen. It offers more than 30 offline vision functions, connects to large language models such as DeepSeek, Doubao and Qwen, and is programmable in Scratch and MicroPython.

item.title: KittenBot AI Speech Recognition (Offline) Robot Puppy Kit
item.description: The AI Speech Recognition Robot Puppy Kit is a micro:bit-based robot dog kit from KittenBot with an offline voice recognition module that wakes the dog by voice and triggers programmed responses. Learners use MakeCode visual programming to map voice commands to movements, turning it into a programmable desktop companion.

item.title: CodeeBot CodeeBot
item.description: CodeeBot is a screen-free coding system from Paiyou Technology, a startup founded at Wuhan University's science park, in which children snap together magnetic blocks that each represent an instruction such as motor control, loops or conditions to program robots and gadgets like a curtain robot. Chips in the blocks let the system read the assembled program, a moving light shows its execution path, and a GPT-based voice tutor gives guidance; it was crowdfunded on Kickstarter in July 2026.

item.title: Hiwonder Tankbot
item.description: Tankbot is an ESP32-driven AI robot from Hiwonder that pairs a suspension tank chassis with a 5+1-DOF robotic arm using inverse kinematics for gripping. It has an RGB ultrasonic sensor, an 8-channel line follower and a WonderLLM AI module for vision and voice interaction.

item.title: Guanggu Shengchuang NAO Mini
item.description: Small educational humanoid robot from Wuhan-based Guanggu Shengchuang, first launched at WRC 2026. It is about 40 cm tall with 18 joint degrees of freedom, has built-in large-language-model voice interaction and a graded programming curriculum, and targets home companionship and K-12 AI education.

item.title: AgileX Robotics Modular ALOHA
item.description: Dual-arm teleoperation platform from AgileX Robotics built on the RANGER MINI 3.0 omnidirectional base with four PiPER 6-DOF arms, three depth cameras, a LiDAR and an RTX 4060 industrial computer. Its split leader-follower design allows cross-space remote teleoperation and adjustable working height for embodied-AI data collection; it was added to AgileX's lineup in July 2026.

item.title: AgileX Robotics RANGER AIR
item.description: Compact four-wheel-drive, four-wheel-steering omnidirectional base from AgileX Robotics designed to carry humanoid upper bodies, dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators for embodied-AI research. It supports lateral movement and zero-radius turns, has a 25 km full-load range and offers CAN, C++ SDK and ROS/ROS 2 interfaces.

item.title: Primo Toys Cubetto+
item.description: Updated version of the Montessori-inspired Cubetto wooden coding robot for children aged 3 and up, programmed screen-free by placing 24 coding blocks on an interface board with an 18-step main sequence plus a 4-step function line. It adds left-to-right program order and USB-C rechargeable batteries rated for about 2 hours of robot play and 10 hours on the board; sold by Primo Toys, now operated by Moravia Consulting in Brno.

item.title: Mobsya Thymio 3
item.description: Thymio 3 is the next-generation version of the open-source Thymio educational robot, designed with EPFL and ECAL and produced by the Swiss nonprofit Mobsya, succeeding the earlier Thymio II (now sold as Thymio 2+). It adds built-in Bluetooth (replacing the old USB dongle), a 3-axis gyroscope and accelerometer for precise geometric movement, a ground-facing RGB color sensor, an audio chip for recording and MP3 playback, and USB-C charging with 3 to 6 hours of runtime, programmed through the thymio.lab coding platform. Pre-orders opened in July 2026 for classroom delivery that September.

item.title: AMZ AI Robotics S1
item.description: The AMZ S1 is a 95 cm tall humanoid classroom robot made by AMZ AI Robotics (Grupo Realms) in Manaus, Brazil, with a chest-mounted tablet, depth camera and 9-axis IMU for autonomous navigation. It runs local AI models of up to 7 billion parameters to teach English and programming (Python, ROS 2, block coding), support reading practice and communicate with autistic students via pictograms. Announced in 2026 with a Manaus production line targeting 200 units in its first year; first deliveries are planned for mid-2027.

item.title: Dobot Magician Go
item.description: DOBOT Magician Go is a mobile robotics platform for STEAM classrooms, designed for interactive STEM education and supporting real-world AI and robotics training in classroom environments, part of Dobot's education product line alongside the Magician and Magician Lite desktop arms.

item.title: Faraday Future Nova
item.description: Nova is an entry-level embodied-AI bipedal humanoid from FF EAI Robotics (a Faraday Future spin-off), aimed at developers, researchers and educators. It is about 50 cm tall, weighs 2.8 kg, has 20 full-body degrees of freedom and a detachable wheeled base, and carries a 2D LiDAR, ~4 MP camera and 3D ToF sensor; it ships with an open SDK and reinforcement-learning (Sim2Real) support, priced from 2,490 USD, with phased preorder access that opened in late 2026.

item.title: Faraday Future Nova Mini
item.description: Nova Mini is a sub-1-kilogram aluminum-alloy bipedal humanoid teaching robot from FF EAI Robotics (a Faraday Future spin-off), built for Physical-AI education aimed at children aged 8 and up. It walks on two legs, turns, balances dynamically and performs forward rolls, and is programmed through visual block-based coding and teaching-by-demonstration; it costs 299 USD for the device plus an optional 499 USD curriculum of 16 live classes, and is aimed at K-12 classrooms, after-school programs and home use.

item.title: Faraday Future Master Mini
item.description: Master Mini is a compact educational humanoid robot from FF EAI Robotics (Faraday Future's robotics division), standing 95 cm tall, weighing 19.5 kg and offering 22 degrees of freedom of full-body coordinated motion. It is pitched as the first compact embodied-AI humanoid in the US to combine programming education, an open development platform (the FF EAI Brain, supporting large speech models and an expandable skills library) and athletic competition use, and starts at 9,990 USD.

item.title: Leju Robot Pando
item.description: Pando is an educational programming robot from Chinese humanoid maker Leju Robotics, offered alongside its general-purpose Kuavo humanoid and small/medium biped Roban lines as part of Leju's educational programming robot series for STEM teaching.

item.title: Vstone Light Rover E32
item.description: Light Rover E32 is a small ROS 2 learning robot from Vstone with a built-in YDLIDAR X2 LiDAR unit. It offloads SLAM and autonomous-navigation computation to an external PC over Wi-Fi (a remote-brain design) to keep the robot itself small, light and inexpensive, and ships assembled with ROS 2 Humble/Jazzy sample code for SLAM and Nav2; its ESP32-S3 control board can also be programmed directly in the Arduino IDE.

item.title: Texas Instruments TI-Rover BT
item.description: TI-Rover BT is a Bluetooth-enabled educational robotic vehicle made by Texas Instruments that pairs wirelessly with a TI-84 Evo graphing calculator (OS 7.1+) via a TI Bluetooth Adapter, letting students write Python programs to drive it and plot lines, parabolas, circles, ellipses and sine/cosine curves with a marker holder (fine/ultra-fine dry-erase marker) on chart paper or dry-erase surfaces, plus a front-mounted ultrasonic ranger and an RGB LED controllable via Python I/O commands. Announced by Texas Instruments on October 22, 2026, it ships with the TI Bluetooth Adapter and is sold through instructional dealers nationwide; TI plans to add TI-Nspire CX II and CX II CAS calculator support in 2027.

item.title: Fischertechnik Robotics High-Tech
item.description: Voice recognition, image processing, building kits

item.title: Petoi Nybble Q
item.description: Open-source programmable robot cat for coding and robotics learning.

item.title: Direct Drive Tech D1
item.description: Direct Drive Tech's fully modular embodied intelligent robot combining bipedal and quadruped locomotion with NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX compute, ROS 2 support and 80 kg standing payload for embodied-AI research and field robotics.

item.title: Hiwonder LanderPi
item.description: LanderPi is a Raspberry Pi 5-based composite ROS 2 education robot from Hiwonder offered with Mecanum, Ackermann or tank chassis. It has a 6-DOF robotic arm with an Aurora930 Pro 3D depth camera at its end, LiDAR for SLAM mapping and navigation, and uses large language and vision-language models for voice-commanded navigation and grasping.

item.title: Hiwonder ROSOrin
item.description: ROSOrin is a ROS 2 multimodal AI robot car from Hiwonder with a modular aluminum chassis that switches between Mecanum, Ackermann and four-wheel differential drive. It runs on NVIDIA Jetson or Raspberry Pi 5 with an STL-19P TOF LiDAR, an Aurora 930 Pro 3D depth camera and a six-microphone array, and is powered by an 11.1 V 6,000 mAh battery.

item.title: Hiwonder miniHexa
item.description: miniHexa is an entry-level hexapod robot from Hiwonder with an ESP32 controller, 18 anti-stall micro servos and built-in inverse kinematics for 360° omnidirectional walking. It includes ultrasonic and IMU sensors, an AI voice interaction module that responds to commands within about 5 m, and supports Arduino programming with open-source code and schematics.

item.title: Yahboom ROSMASTER M3 Pro
item.description: ROSMASTER M3 Pro is an embodied-AI ROS 2 robot platform from Yahboom for ROS education, research experiments and AI teaching, built on a Mecanum-wheel chassis with pendulum suspension. It integrates multimodal large language models for voice interaction, vision recognition and tracking.

item.title: Yahboom ROSMASTER A1
item.description: ROSMASTER A1 is a ROS 2 educational robot car from Yahboom with an Ackermann steering chassis and AI large-language-model integration.

item.title: Yahboom ROSMASTER M1
item.description: ROSMASTER M1 is an omnidirectional Mecanum-wheel ROS2 robot from Yahboom for robotics education and AI research, supporting Raspberry Pi 5, RDK X5, Jetson Nano or Jetson Orin Nano. It can carry lidar, a 3D depth camera and an AI voice module for SLAM navigation and multimodal large-model interaction.

item.title: Jaka Robotics Lumi
item.description: Embodied-intelligence training platform from JAKA launched in China in May 2025 for schools, research institutes and developers. It combines a six-axis arm (2 kg load), two vision cameras, a lifting waist (0-400 mm), a rotating neck and a mobile platform for 12 degrees of freedom, measures 510 x 510 x 1460-1860 mm and weighs 95.6 kg.

item.title: WhalesBot Pubbo Air
item.description: Interactive STEM robot for children aged 4 to 12 from WhalesBot that can be played with directly, driven with a controller or programmed through the Pubbo app, which provides lessons, missions and online competitions. It has multiple sensors and expressive displays.

item.title: BSG and Technologies IRIS
item.description: IRIS is a wheeled humanoid AI tutor robot with a chest-mounted screen and speakers, developed by South African company BSG and Technologies (founded by Bonisiwe "Thandoh" Gumede) in partnership with Indian robotics firm MakerLabs, and publicly launched in Durban in August 2025. It uses natural language processing, voice interaction and adaptive learning to teach subjects from Grade R through tertiary level in all 11 of South Africa's official languages. As of August 2026 it was running in five KwaZulu-Natal schools on donated units, with parts cut in India and assembled at Durban's Dube TradePort; the national science department has publicly endorsed the project but has not funded it.

item.title: Rice University XLeRobot
item.description: XLeRobot is an open-source household dual-arm mobile robot created by Gaotian 'Vector' Wang at Rice University's RobotPi Lab, combining two 3D-printed SO-100/SO-101 arms (from Hugging Face's LeRobot ecosystem) with an omni-wheel mobile base and an IKEA cart frame. It costs about 660 USD to build, assembles in under 4 hours, weighs about 12 kg and runs over 10 hours per charge, aimed at robotics education, embodied-AI research and DIY developers.

item.title: RoboRobo UARO
item.description: UARO is RoboRobo's first coding robot for preschoolers, letting children assemble a model with simple tools and then program it with block-based coding to learn early computational thinking.

item.title: Sphero Bolt+
item.description: LCD screen, 6 programmable LEDs, Qi wireless charging, waterproof, 38 lessons

item.title: Elecfreaks Smart Cutebot Pro
item.description: micro:bit robot car, closed-loop N20 motors (300 rpm), 4-ch line tracking, ultrasonic, 18650 battery

item.title: Yahboom Raspbot V2
item.description: Raspberry Pi 5 AI car, mecanum wheels, 2-DOF camera gimbal, OpenCV/MediaPipe vision, LLM voice AI

item.title: Arduino Alvik
item.description: Nano ESP32 robot, ToF+color+line sensors, 6-axis IMU, LEGO Technic mounts, MicroPython/blocks, 0.41 kg

item.title: WhalesBot AI Module 5
item.description: Sensor-rich coding robot kit teaching Scratch, C and Python.

item.title: Waveshare UGV Rover
item.description: UGV Rover is an open-source six-wheel, four-wheel-drive AI robot from Waveshare with an all-metal body and a dual-controller design: a Raspberry Pi 4B/5 host for vision and ROS 2 plus an ESP32 sub-controller for motion control, IMU and battery monitoring. It reaches 0.5 m/s and accepts a pan-tilt camera, LiDAR and accessory rails; the base kit was listed at 244.99 USD.

item.title: KittenBot TabbyBot
item.description: TabbyBot is a micro:bit-programmed STEM robot car kit from Shenzhen-based KittenBot powered by an 18650 lithium battery that can drive add-ons such as AI camera and voice-recognition modules. It has programmable LEDs and RGB lights, line-following, infrared and ultrasonic sensors, servo and motor drivers, four expansion ports and LEGO-compatible mounting holes.

item.title: Hiwonder JetAcker
item.description: JetAcker is an Ackermann-steering ROS robot car from Hiwonder for autonomous-driving education, powered by an NVIDIA Jetson controller with lidar, a 3D depth camera, a microphone array and an HD display. It supports mapping, path planning, obstacle avoidance and large-model voice interaction.

item.title: Hiwonder MentorPi M1
item.description: MentorPi M1 is a Raspberry Pi 5-powered ROS2 robot car from Hiwonder with a Mecanum-wheel chassis, closed-loop encoder motors, lidar and a 3D depth camera. It supports SLAM mapping, path planning, YOLO-based traffic-sign detection and a multimodal large AI model.

item.title: Hiwonder TurboPi
item.description: TurboPi is a beginner Raspberry Pi robot car from Hiwonder with a Mecanum-wheel chassis and a 2-DOF HD wide-angle camera pan-tilt. It is programmed in Python with OpenCV and YOLO for color recognition, object tracking and autonomous driving, with ROS2 and large-model voice options in higher kits.

item.title: Freenove Bipedal Robot Kit for Raspberry Pi Pico (FNK0033)
item.description: Freenove Bipedal Robot Kit is a small two-legged walking robot kit controlled by a Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico W, with an LED-matrix face, obstacle avoidance, colored lights, buzzer and speaker. It is assembled by the user and supports app and IR remote control.

item.title: AgileX Robotics COBOT MAGIC
item.description: Open-source whole-body teleoperation platform from AgileX Robotics (松灵机器人) based on Stanford's Mobile ALOHA architecture. It combines a TRACER 2.0 mobile base with four 6-DOF PiPER arms (two leader, two follower), wrist and top-view cameras and an onboard PC for bimanual manipulation, demonstration-data collection and VLA model training.

item.title: ZeroBionic Ubuntu-12
item.description: Ubuntu-12 is a 3D-printed robotic arm made by Kenyan startup ZeroBionic, founded by Norah Kimathi, that translates a teacher's spoken STEM lessons into sign language for deaf students in real time and uses computer vision to read students' signing back into text. Printed largely from recycled plastic, each unit costs about 350 USD, works offline, and the company reports roughly 92 percent speech-to-sign translation accuracy across more than 150 classroom pilots in Africa.

item.title: AgileX Robotics LIMO COBOT
item.description: LIMO COBOT is a ROS 2 mobile-manipulation education platform from AgileX Robotics, pairing a reconfigurable 4-motion-mode mobile base (5.6 kg payload) with a lightweight 6-DoF robotic arm (250 g arm payload). It runs on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with EAI T-mini Pro LiDAR, an Orbbec Astra+ depth camera and an IMU for SLAM and dynamic obstacle avoidance, and lasts about 2.5 hours per charge.

item.title: MatataStudio VinciBot
item.description: 8 sensors, 18x6 LED panel, Scratch & Python, LEGO compatible, IR remote, line tracking, drawing, voice control
